sections.h2: Stay on the right side of the sites

body.p: Reading a public pricing page once a day is what any customer does. Stay on public pages, check no more than you need, and respect robots.txt. If a page needs a login or shows a CAPTCHA, take that as a no.
In the US, hiQ v. LinkedIn treated scraping public data as likely lawful, with a line at data behind a login. Site terms still apply, and laws differ by country.

method.h2: How to monitor competitor prices automatically, step by step

steps.title: List the pages and prices
steps.body: One row per price: competitor, page, plan, and the price now. That first price is your baseline.

steps.title: Pick a time of day and keep it
steps.body: Same time each day, so a change shows on the day it happened.

steps.title: Store the last price seen
steps.body: Each check compares with the last price, then replaces it. Without this, you get the same alert every day.

steps.title: Alert only on change, with both numbers
steps.body: "Acme Team plan: $29 to $35" is useful; a daily "all checked" is noise. Name the billing period, so monthly and yearly never get mixed up.

steps.title: Alert on failures separately
steps.body: Page did not load, price not found, layout changed: each says so in its own alert.

note.text: A silent failure looks exactly like "no change". If nothing has changed for a month, open one page yourself.

steps.title: Review the list monthly
steps.body: Competitors rename plans and move pages. Update the list when they do.

captain.line: Captain sets up a browser agent that opens your list each morning in its own browser, reads the prices, and tells you what changed or what it could not read.

wrong.title: The same alert every day
wrong.body: The stored price was never replaced after the first alert. Store the new price each time.

wrong.title: Noise from promotions
wrong.body: A weekend sale triggers two alerts. Say whether you care about sale prices, and label them as such.

wrong.title: Blocked or challenged
wrong.body: You checked too often, or the site does not want bots. Check less, and drop any page that shows a bot check.

wrong.title: A plan renamed
wrong.body: The competitor renamed Team to Business, and the price reads as gone. Treat "plan not found" as a prompt to update the list.

faqs.q: Is it legal to monitor competitor prices?
faqs.a: Reading public pricing pages is common and, in the US, was treated as likely lawful in hiQ v. LinkedIn. Respect site terms, avoid anything behind a login or a CAPTCHA, and check the law where you operate.

faqs.q: How often should I check competitor prices?
faqs.a: Daily is enough for most businesses. Retail catalogues with frequent repricing may need more, which is what dedicated price trackers are built for.

faqs.q: Is there a free way to do it?
faqs.a: For a few pages, a weekly check by hand. Pricefy's free plan covers up to 50 SKUs and 5 competitors with one update a day.
